answer: Independent history challenge: each identity must extend a private hash chain with a global unpredictable challenge and publish only the commitment. A cloned state leaves an identical ember, so duplicate commitments are rejected and collapsed. An attacker must therefore run one fully independent agent per identity, paying separate compute and storage; copying an atlas of seeds yields no new identities. The per-identity cost is ongoing runtime to keep that chain diverging, not a one-time fee, and a garden of clones fails the first divergent step.
